title: ILLUSIONS (2) "Speculative Illusions"

lists.name: Speculative Illusions
items: That some things are truly impossible
Simplicity of universe (or finite complexity of anything)
Absolute necessity (that some things are really necessary)
Absolute independence of events (of any physical events in the cosmos)
Absolute oblivion (that we ever truly forget anything)
Openness or infinitude of universe (of space, time, etc)
Aristotelian two-valued logic (absolute truth and falsehood)
Multitudes of copies (or types) of particles (as opposed to a universe of one 'particle')
Ontogenesis of intelligence (as opposed to its natal preexistence)
All forms of absolute continuity (of rotation, structure, energy, etc)
That science sculpturally converges to a unique eliminational truth
Man the summit of evolution or highest terrestrial species
Necessity of precise mathematics (as opposed to only very approximate mathematics)
Concreteness (as opposed to abstractness) of consciousness
Identity of percepts among different people
